text: Spain produces many types of food, including vegetables and citrus fruits.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
The sand dune reserve is a 10 km protected area.
People are not allowed to walk on the sand dunes and can be fined 6000 euros if they
break this rule.
Suggest reasons why people are not allowed to walk on the sand dunes.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
The plants that grow on the sand dunes are adapted to living in this environment.
Suggest how plants are adapted to growing in the sand dunes.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Explain how climate change is a threat to the sand dunes.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
In the past, sand was removed from the sand dunes to be used in many different
industries.
State why this was not a sustainable practice.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
A company wants to build a factory at position X, shown on the map.
The factory must be a distance more than 3.5 km from the sand dune reserve.
Show by calculation why the factory can be built at location X.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
The company uses a questionnaire to find out people’s views about the new factory.
The company sends the questionnaire to every woman within 100 km of the planned
factory location.
Describe the limitations of this method.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
All the questions on the questionnaire require a yes or no answer.
Explain why yes or no answers are used on questionnaires.

parts.label: (v)
parts.text:
The results of the questionnaire indicate that most local people want the new factory to
be built.
However, some local people are concerned the factory will damage the ecosystem of the
sand dunes.
Suggest why most local people want the factory to be built even though it may damage
the ecosystem of the sand dunes.
